financials.source: CommonSpirit Health FY2024 (ending June 30, 2024) annual report and Fitch October 2025 rating report. Total operating revenues $37,517M as reported. Operating loss $581M (-1.5% margin). Total assets $54,734M; total liabilities $32,482M; net assets $22,252M. FY2025 as reported: revenue $39,116M, operating loss $687M (-1.8% margin), total assets $57,260M, net assets $23,573M.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Long-term investments excluding assets limited as to use at June 30, 2024 per CommonSpirit FY2025 annual report comparison column. FY2025 value was $14,490M. Unrestricted cash and investments totaled $16.8B at June 30, 2025. Investment allocation (June 30, 2025 per S&P): 43% equities, 35% private equity/hedge funds/other, 22% fixed income/cash.
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: Not verified. CommonSpirit operates 137 hospital-based locations and 2,300+ clinics across 24 states. In California, Dignity Health operates approximately 39 hospitals.
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Consolidated net assets $22,252M at June 30, 2024 and $23,573M at June 30, 2025. Parent entity (EIN 86-1223604) reported net assets of $14,410,705,805 as of June 2024 per ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Investment income net was $1,719M in FY2025 and $2,401M in FY2026. Endowment net assets were $317M (FY2025) and $322M (FY2026). Total cash and investments $20,460M at June 30, 2025. The 49ers partnership operates through Dignity Health, the legacy California operating entity of CommonSpirit.

bondDebt.largestIssueProceeds: $2,300,000,000 taxable; plus $504,100,000 WA tax-exempt (Series 2025A) and $514,000,000 CO tax-exempt (Series 2025A)
bondDebt.issuerAuthority: Washington Health Care Facilities Authority; Colorado Health Facilities Authority; California Health Facilities Financing Authority
bondDebt.source: S&P Global Ratings report September 26, 2025; Bond Buyer reporting. Pre-merger combined debt was approximately $13.7B ($8.5B CHI + $5.2B Dignity Health). Post-merger 2019 refinancing issued $6.5B in tax-exempt and taxable debt. All debt secured under CommonSpirit master trust indenture (MTI) with gross receivable pledge of the obligated group. California Dignity Health facilities are part of the obligated group.

relatedOrganizations.source: Schedule R; CommonSpirit formed in 2019 from merger of Catholic Health Initiatives and Dignity Health. Operates 137 hospital-based locations and 2,300+ clinics in 24 states. 157,000+ employees, 45,000 nurses, 25,000 physicians. The 49ers partnership is branded through Dignity Health, the legacy California entity that merged into CommonSpirit in 2019.

executiveComp.source: Wright Lassiter III serves as CEO. 990 aggregator RoundPaper reports $14,175,319 total comp for Lassiter from CommonSpirit Health Operating Investment (EIN 85-0919176) tax year 2024; Paddock Post reports $15,397,051 from Dignity Health subsidiary filing for 2024. Parent entity EIN 86-1223604 shows $1,454,414 for 2023 per Paddock Post, likely reflecting holding company allocation only. Total officer compensation across all CommonSpirit entities reported at $129.6M (3.3% of total expenses). Individual comp breakdowns left null due to conflicting figures across multiple related EINs.

communityBenefit.source: CommonSpirit FY2025 annual report (comparison column for FY2024). Total community benefits $2,574M (FY2024), $3,071M (FY2025). Charity care at customary charges $2,169M (FY2024), $2,659M (FY2025). Charity care at cost net $559M (FY2024), $680M (FY2025). Including unpaid cost of Medicare: $4,221M (FY2024), $5,156M (FY2025). Community service to poor $143M (FY2024). Chargemaster markup ratio computed as $2,169M charges / $559M cost = 3.88x. Cost-to-charge ratio = $559M / $2,169M = 0.258. California requires SB 697 community benefit reporting for nonprofit hospitals.

taxAdvantage.notes: CommonSpirit holds massive tax-exempt bond portfolios through multiple state health facility authorities including California, Colorado, and Washington. Total tax advantage across 24-state, 137-hospital system is substantial but not quantified here. California Dignity Health hospitals benefit from property tax exemptions under the state welfare exemption.

layoffs.description: Cut approximately 2,000 full-time equivalents in ancillary, support, and overhead functions in Q4 FY2023, alongside undisclosed leadership and administrative layoffs in Q3 FY2023. System posted $1.4 billion operating loss for FY2023.
layoffs.source: Becker's Hospital Review; Fierce Healthcare; Healthcare Dive

layoffs.description: 175+ healthcare staff across CommonSpirit Dignity Health facilities in California received layoff notices, including nearly 60 workers at Bakersfield Memorial Hospital. Affected positions included nurses, patient transporters, physical therapy aides, telemetry technicians, unit assistants, and clerks.
layoffs.source: National Nurses United; Bakersfield Now; SEIU-UHW

Post-merger operational alignment of CHI and Dignity Health legacy systems
Moody's upgraded from Baa1 to A3 in February 2024 reflecting improved performance
Heavy reliance on non-operating investment returns to offset operating losses

Virginia Mason in Seattle affiliated with CommonSpirit; debt incorporated under master trust indenture

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Investment portfolio of $13.3B is 22.8x the $581M FY2024 operating loss. Investment income net of $1,719M in FY2025 was 2.5x the $687M operating loss that year, meaning investment returns substantially exceed and mask operating deficits.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Total outstanding debt of $19.8B is 7.7x the $2,574M community benefit claimed in FY2024. Tax-exempt bond interest subsidies on this debt portfolio likely exceed the charity care cost of $559M.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Charity care at cost ($559M) was 1.4% of total expenses in FY2024, rising to 1.7% in FY2025. California state average not verified.

accusation: CommonSpirit Health sits on $54.7 billion in total assets -- including a $13.3 billion investment portfolio and $22.3 billion in net assets -- while carrying $19.8 billion in tax-advantaged debt. The system posted a $581 million operating loss in fiscal 2024 and a $687 million loss in fiscal 2025, yet earned $1.7 billion in net investment income in FY2025 alone, using Wall Street returns to paper over clinical operating deficits. It claimed $2.6 billion in community benefit while its charity care at actual cost was just $559 million -- a 3.88x chargemaster markup inflating the headline figure. Meanwhile, its Dignity Health subsidiary serves as the San Francisco 49ers' official healthcare partner at Levi's Stadium, and CommonSpirit cut 2,000 jobs in FY2023 and issued 175+ layoff notices at California Dignity Health hospitals in 2026, all while maintaining tax-exempt status across 137 hospitals in 24 states.
